cover.headline: Stolen AI keys from one breach ran up about *$740,000*.
cover.sub: Railway's attacker went for AI provider keys first. Five moves from 10 Nov that change a builder's week, plus two free courses.

items.title: Railway's attacker went for the *AI keys* first
items.statLabel: of AI usage on stolen keys, Railway's estimate
items.what: An attacker partly escaped a shared build machine on 20 Oct, then decrypted customer variables. Up to about 100,000 workspaces may be exposed.
items.why: Refunds depend on who issued the key: Bedrock and Gemini cover fraud, OpenAI decides case by case, OpenRouter has a no-refund policy. Cap every key.

items.title: A breach at Fireworks exposed *Notion AI* chats
items.statLabel: of Notion workspaces, most chats with no user or workspace label
items.what: Fireworks served open-weight models for Notion. Attackers reached its machines through a cloud provider on 24 Oct. Notion has cut Fireworks off.
items.why: Your vendor's vendors hold your data too. Fireworks says its zero-retention inference shows no impact so far. The stored data was what got hit.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is out. The price *doubles* on 1 Dec
items.statLabel: per 1M input tokens from 1 Dec, up from $2. Output: $10 to $20
items.what: Google's model for cyber work and long agent runs opened to paid API users on 10 Nov. Google reports #1 on CursorBench 4.0 and AutomationBench.
items.why: Google says Argon still suits most work and Carbon spends more tokens. Cost any pilot at $4 and $20, not at the launch price.

items.title: Claude gets Sheets. Claude Data goes *default-on*
items.statLabel: when Claude Data turns on by default for Enterprise
items.what: Sheets and Whiteboards are in beta on all paid plans and export to .xlsx, CSV, docs or decks. Claude Data, formerly Dashboards, is now GA.
items.why: Admins can scope each connector, say read Slack but never send, and set spend limits. Decide your Claude Data setting before 19 Nov.

items.title: New York: report AI incidents within *72 hours*
items.statLabel: to report a critical safety incident, for labs above $500M revenue
items.what: RAISE Act registration opened on 10 Nov. Large frontier developers must register by 1 Jan 2027 and publish safety frameworks. Fines reach $3M.
items.why: It binds your model vendor, not your app. Its regulator sits inside NY's financial regulator. Ask vendors how fast you would hear of an incident.

courses.title: Learn Agentic Coding with Codex
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, about 2 hours, posted 10 Nov. Includes using Git safely with an agent and protecting API keys and secrets.

courses.title: The Anatomy of an AI Data Center
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, 8 hours, posted 16 Oct. Power, cooling and networking, then GPU cloud economics and capacity contracts.

readTitle: An AI key is a *card number* now
read: Whoever holds it can *spend on it*, and the issuer decides whether you get the money back. One breach put about *$740,000* on stolen keys. Guard AI keys the way a payments team guards card numbers.
takeaway: Give every AI key a cap, an owner and a revocation plan.
